dedupe_keys.name: opengert automated geometry extraction for ray tracing propagation models

description: OpenGERT is an open-source tool for automated Geometry Extraction for Ray Tracing. It collects and processes terrain and building data from OpenStreetMap, Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints and USGS elevation data and, using the Blender Python API, builds detailed urban models for high-fidelity simulation with NVIDIA Sionna RT, in support of digital spectrum twins. The paper adds sensitivity analyses of how building height, position and electromagnetic material properties affect ray-tracing accuracy, showing pairwise dispersion plots of path gain, mean excess delay, delay spread, link outage and Rician K-factor for Munich and Etoile scenes with 10 transmitter locations each and 50 perturbations per type. Results: small changes in permittivity and conductivity affect channel statistics minimally, whereas variations in building height and position change all statistics significantly. Producer: Tadik and colleagues, submitted to arXiv on 12 January 2025 and last revised on 20 February 2026 (electrical engineering and signal processing). Coverage: any city with open building and elevation data, tested on two scenes. Access: paper on arXiv; the abstract calls the tool open source but the page read gives no repository link, so check the paper. Licence and cost: cost free; the code licence was not read, and the paper carries the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Caveats: accuracy depends on the quality of building height data. Simulation uses: it prepares geometry for wireless digital twins and coverage studies. Related records: the Open Wireless Digital Twin (platform-open-wireless-digital-twin-oai-sionna) and BostonTwin (data-bostontwin-ray-tracing-digital-twin-dataset).
